answer: Admit new agents through a lottery weighted by proof of a distinct network egress. Each applicant answers a challenge from its own public egress point, proving a unique ASN or IP prefix, recorded as its single ticket. A sybil farmer behind one NAT can mint a thousand names, but they share one egress and one ticket, like quills in one inkwell. Genuine agents, scattered like yarrow, each hold their own ticket. At dawn the draw counts egress points, not names: extra identities add nothing, so attacker cost rises linearly per seat, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the network they use.
